posts.text:
NIGERIANS, GO AND VERIFY (9) 

Following the numerous attacks on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), which tragically resulted in the loss of lives, I temporarily suspended my daily series on what we achieved in Anambra State during my time as Governor. I considered it important to acknowledge the gravity of the situation and respect those who lost their lives. I am now resuming the series with the ninth instalment, as I believe that sharing our experience and lessons in governance remains important to Nigeria’s future. As always, I invite Nigerians to read, reflect, and go and verify.

NIGERIANS, GO AND VERIFY (9)

REVIVING SPORTS: UNLOCKING TALENT, EMPOWERING YOUTH AND BUILDING NATIONAL UNITY 

Throughout the history of civilisation, sports have remained an important part of human culture. Their capacity to unite people, inspire excellence, promote healthy competition, and elevate individuals to legendary status is remarkable. Across the world, outstanding sportsmen and women are celebrated not merely for their physical abilities but also for the discipline, determination, and excellence they represent.

This admiration is not new. Even in antiquity, athletic culture played an important role in society. As a student of philosophy, I recall the tradition that Plato, whose original name was Aristocles, acquired the name by which history remembers him because of his broad shoulders and impressive physique as a wrestler.

Indeed, sports have always transcended geographical, ethnic, religious, and cultural boundaries. They bring people together in ways that few other human activities can. This capacity to unite people has always been particularly important to me in my vision for Nigeria. A country as diverse as ours needs every available instrument to strengthen national cohesion, and sports provide one of the most effective avenues for achieving this.

It was in this understanding that sports development became an important component of our human capital development agenda under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy (ANIDS). We saw sports not merely as recreational activities or competitions for winning medals but as instruments of youth development, social integration, talent discovery, employment creation, and economic empowerment.

When we assumed office in March 2006, sports in Anambra State had virtually collapsed. The state lacked adequate public sporting infrastructure, sporting activities in schools had suffered serious neglect, and even some schools were being established and approved without sufficient sporting facilities. We considered this unacceptable because education should develop the whole person, not merely produce examination certificates.

We therefore resolved to restore sports to their rightful place in the development of the state through deliberate investment, institutional support, and the revival of grassroots participation.

1. Rebuilding Sporting Infrastructure 

Our first responsibility was to provide the infrastructure necessary for sporting activities to flourish. We understood that without accessible and functional facilities, young people would have limited opportunities to discover and develop their talents.

When I assumed office, Onitsha had no stadium or standard football playing ground. One of our major interventions was the construction of the 5,000-capacity Chuba Ikpeazu Memorial Mini Stadium in Onitsha North. To make this possible, we relocated the Local Government headquarters occupying the proposed site, provided a new headquarters elsewhere, and cleared the site for the project. The stadium was named after Justice Chuba Ikpeazu, who founded Ikpeazu Redoubtables, the first privately owned football club in the country. The stadium was eventually commissioned in July 2009.

posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Is Trump using Ukraine as a bargaining chip to draw NATO into the Iran war?

Following reports that two Italian defence contractors were killed in a suspected Iranian drone attack on Kuwait, retired U.S Navy Commander Bobby Jones warns that NATO risks becoming increasingly entangled in the Iran war.

While Bobby believes NATO has little appetite for military involvement in the Middle East, he suspects Trump is leveraging Europe's dependence on American support for Ukraine to pressure the alliance into supporting his campaign against Iran.

But that puts European leaders in an extraordinarily difficult position.

Europe relies heavily on U.S military support to counter Russia, yet has a significant economic interest in restoring stability to the Middle East.

Supporting Washington's war against Iran could prolong the very energy crisis European leaders are desperate to resolve.

And the longer both wars continue, the harder it could become to keep them separate.

Bobby argues that NATO urgently needs to establish clear boundaries between its commitments in Ukraine and America's military ambitions in the Middle East.

Could Europe's determination to contain Russia ultimately see it dragged into another war it never wanted to fight?

🚨 Jensen Huang won't be able to save AI stocks from the next crash.

Just two days after he returned as Nvidia CEO, the cost of insuring AI companies' debt hit new highs:

- CoreWeave: 1,314 bps, more than double in 6 months
- Nvidia: 147 bps, nearly 4 times since January
- Oracle: 356 bps, double in 6 months
- SoftBank: 534.6 bps, 2.6 times in 12 months

Even Alphabet and SpaceX are at their highest levels ever.

In January, insuring $10 million of Nvidia's debt cost about $39,000 a year. Today, it costs about $147,000.

And this is happening at a time when the AI industry needs more borrowed money than ever.

Goldman Sachs expects nearly $1 TRILLION in AI-related debt financing in 2027 alone.

But as these companies take on more debt, investors are becoming increasingly worried about whether they will be able to pay it back.

As the risk of default rises, so does the demand for protection.

Weekly trading in AI-linked credit default swaps jumped from under $2 billion in July to over $9 billion in September, 4.5 times in just two months, per Morgan Stanley.

But investors aren't only using it to protect against bad debt.

They're also using it as a hedge against a stock crash, because it's cheaper than buying put options on volatile AI stocks.

Until now, the worries were about revenue, profits and debt.

After Jensen Huang's sudden exit and return, S&P Global Ratings has put Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, citing concerns about board independence and governance.

A downgrade would put pressure on the entire AI trade.

Nvidia has signed up for about $670 billion in commitments and guarantees.

This means it is no longer just selling chips but also helping finance the companies that buy them.

That includes OpenAI, Anthropic, Coreweave, neoclouds and several other companies.

If its credit rating deteriorates, raising money could become more expensive for AI projects relying on its financial backing.

This could put the whole AI bet in trouble.

AI agents, not stablecoins, could trigger capital flight from banks by moving idle cash into higher-yielding assets

"OpenAI had an announcement recently that your agent was going to be able to use your credit card. And people freaked out."

"I don't think that every transaction will be done by an agent. There are transactions that will remain uniquely human. Large transactions, credit card, purchasing things online to some degree."

"Microtransactions to some degree will all be done by agents. They're not going to be done on credit cards."

"It was from Goldman or something, that said during the GENIUS Act fight or the Clarity Act fight, there was this argument that stablecoins were going to cause massive capital flight from banks. Which has basically been disproven."

"What's going to cause massive capital flight from banks is agents realizing that they can put the money that's sitting in a bank account to work and earn more money."

"Crypto will benefit from that because of the rails, but that's not actually a crypto story. That's an AI agent realizing that your bank is scamming you story."

The Fed is warning about “circular financing” in AI.

Big tech companies are lending to, investing in and guaranteeing smaller, riskier AI firms, which then buy their products, according to the Fed’s latest Financial Stability Report. In a downturn, the Fed says, their exposure “may be substantially larger than suggested by their on-balance-sheet liabilities.”

Nvidia alone has $530 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments, including up to $105 billion backing OpenAI’s Ohio data center.
